newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ debt markets end mixed after quiet day.
newsitem.headline: NZ debt markets end mixed after quiet day.

text.p: Figures in brackets compare against yesterday's close
FUTURES PHYSICAL YIELD (PCT)
90-DAY BILLS (MAR) 92.29 (PREV 92.28) 90-DAYS 7.67 (PREV 7.70)
OVERNIGHT CASH 7.35 PCT (PREV 7.50) US 5-YR 6.46 (PREV 6.39)
* NZ debt ends mixed after day of minimal volumes
* Bonds sell on U.S. weakness, bills rally
* U.S. non-farm payrolls expected to set scene for next week
New Zealand bonds sold off on thin volumes at Friday's close after getting off to a bad start on the back of U.S. Treasuries' weakness.
Dealers said bearish sentiment in the U.S. going into tonight's February non-farm payrolls data had taken a grip on local bonds, which closed four to five points weaker.
The 7/97 bond was the exception, taking heart from money market strength and ending only one point weaker at 7.58 percent.
Dealers said trading had been light and few people were prepared to take positions ahead of the payrolls data.

"Sentiment is still quite poor. You need a better than expected number in the U.S. -- their market is obviously still concerned about (Federal Reserve Chairman Alan) Greenspan's talk of a pre-emptive tightening, and our market is simply taking that sentiment into its own trading as well," one said.
A money market dealer said the U.S. seemed like it might be oversold, and there was a potential for a rally on a favourable number.
He said there had been a general lack of interest during the local session.
"We've seen people out there picking for value, a little bit of interest in buying the physicals, but there has also been a bit of pressure on the futures."
The 90-day bank bills ended three basis points stronger at 7.67 percent but the front futures contract was only one stronger at 92.29.
